expectedUsable: The heading outline is sequential (h1 → h2 …) so screen-reader users navigating by heading get a coherent document structure.

violations.expectedFix: Change the three section headings from <h4> to <h2> so the outline goes h1 → h2 without skipping levels; style with CSS rather than by choosing a level.
violations.notes: Empirically, NEITHER engine flags this as a conformance failure: axe's heading-order rule is best-practice (excluded from the WCAG-tagged scan) and pa11y/HTMLCS emits only a *warning* (1_3_1_A.G141), not an error. Since Layer A counts definite failures only (axe violations + pa11y errors), heading-skip passes Layer A — a stronger thesis result than expected. Layer B catches it via a deterministic heading-outline traversal (detecting the h1→h4 jump).
